title: Robotic process automation
summary:
Robotic process automation (RPA) is a form of business process automation that is based on software robots (bots) or artificial intelligence (AI) agents. It should not be confused with artificial intelligence as it is based on automation technology following a predefined workflow.

The hosting of RPA services aligns with the metaphor of a software robot, with each robotic instance having its own virtual workstation, much like a human worker. The robot uses keyboard and mouse controls to take actions and execute automations in a virtual environment, interpreting the screen display electronically. The critical difference between RPA and AI is that RPA is process-driven whereas AI is data-driven. RPA bots can follow only the processes defined by an end user, while AI bots use machine learning to recognize patterns in data.

RPA is used in most industries, particularly those that include repetitive tasks such as insurance, banking, finance, healthcare, and telecommunications. In financial services, RPA automates governance, reconciles accounts, processes invoices, manages audit requests, and processes insurance claims. In healthcare, RPA automates appointment scheduling, account management, claims administration, billing, regulatory compliance, and electronic records management.

According to Harvard Business Review, most operations groups adopting RPA have promised their employees that automation would not result in layoffs, with workers redeployed to more interesting work. Although not directly attributable to RPA alone, Oxford University conjectures that up to 35% of all jobs might be automated by 2035. As artificial intelligence has advanced, RPA has expanded beyond automating repetitive tasks to become an essential capability for agentic automation, a new form of automation that leverages intelligent AI agents that can plan, adapt, and make decisions autonomously.
